venues.d: A twelve-acre canyon hideaway of swan lakes and secret gardens: Los Angeles at its most private.

venues.n: The Beverly Hills Hotel, Dorchester Collection
venues.d: The Pink Palace on Sunset since 1912: the definitive myth of Beverly Hills, still gracious.
A gleaming Pierre-Yves Rochon tower at Wilshire and Santa Monica: the marque's West Coast debut.
The group's flawless Californian house: the only Forbes Five-Star, AAA Five-Diamond hotel in Southern California, year after year.
The London group's Californian address: Claridge's polish, a block from Rodeo Drive.

venues.n: Beverly Wilshire, Beverly Hills, A Four Seasons Hotel
venues.d: A 1928 landmark at the foot of Rodeo Drive: grand-hotel bones, Four Seasons hands.

venues.n: Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills
venues.d: The surest hands in Los Angeles: a leafy, low-key garden hotel on Doheny Drive.
The longest-tenured all-suite Forbes Five-Star hotel in the world: discreet, residential calm.
A sixteen-room teak ryokan on Billionaire's Beach: the ocean at the foot of the bed.
The most storied hotel in Hollywood: a Loire-château fantasy above the Sunset Strip.
A sleek Sunset Strip tower with a rooftop over the whole city: contemporary and buzzing.
Ian Schrager's white, garden-wrapped tower: quiet-luxury calm with a rooftop and a basement club.
An Art Deco icon of the Sunset Strip: old-Hollywood glamour, discreetly kept alive.
A Cape-Cod beach house right on the sand: the ocean-side heart of Santa Monica.
A restored 1920s beach club on the sand: a grander, more romantic Santa Monica landmark.
A palm-shaded estate above the ocean bluffs: private bungalows and a century of history.
A turquoise Art Deco jewel newly reborn on Ocean Avenue: glamour with an ocean view.
Kelly Wearstler's sun-bleached, texture-rich design hotel a block from the beach.
A 1920s landmark reborn as Kelly Wearstler's living museum: the coolest room downtown.
A members'-club hotel in the heart of Hollywood: a rooftop pool and a fashionable crowd.
An intimate, design-forward hideaway in the hills above Hollywood: small and personal.
A hilltop 1920s mansion turned private hotel: a Mediterranean villa above the city.
A residential-style boutique house on a quiet WeHo street: apartment-living ease.
A cluster of English-cottage bungalows once home to Charlie Chaplin's circle: private and green.
Michael Cimarusti's temple to seafood: Los Angeles's most decorated table, newly at three stars.
Aitor Zabala's intimate fourteen-seat counter: the first three-star ever awarded in LA County.
Niki Nakayama's modern kaiseki: the most quietly revered tasting menu in Los Angeles.
Brandon Go's eight-seat kaiseki hidden in the Arts District: Kyoto exactitude in Los Angeles.
Josiah Citrin's long-held two-star: contemporary French of great polish, on the Westside.
Jon Yao's Taiwanese-American tasting menu: personal, precise, and among the city's very best.
Nancy Silverton's Italian benchmark: the mozzarella bar and pasta that set the LA standard.
The most glamorous steakhouse in America: Wolfgang Puck's starred room in the Beverly Wilshire.
Josef Centeno's intimate Italian-Japanese tasting counter: a quiet downtown gem.
A ten-seat contemporary Korean counter: global technique on a Korean foundation.
Jordan Kahn's fire-driven, live-flame cooking: theatrical, primal, singular.
Kevin Meehan's seasonal Californian cooking: refined, ingredient-led, unshowy.
An eight-seat sushi counter with fish flown from Japan multiple times a week: newly starred.
A hidden ten-seat omakase behind Sugarfish: pure, classic edomae sushi.
A Valley omakase counter of great purity: quiet mastery away from the Westside crowds.
A basement counter of exacting edomae sushi: a serious, hushed omakase downtown.
An intimate sushi counter on Sawtelle's Japantown strip: refined and personal.
A precise Japanese counter that earned its star with quiet, seasonal craft.
An intimate Italian tasting counter in the Valley: pasta as a tasting menu.
Gilberto Cetina's Yucatán seafood counter: ceviches and tostadas good enough for a star.
Jordan Kahn's futuristic tasting menu in a Gehry-adjacent glass tower: dining as art installation.
An Indian-American sports bar that became LA's most loved crossover: tandoori spaghetti and cricket on the screens.
The fiery southern-Thai institution of LA's Thai Town: decades deep and still unrivalled.
Bright, modern Taiwanese home cooking in an airy room: fresh, fast, beloved.
Chris Bianco's LA outpost: widely called the best pizza in America, now downtown.
Nancy Silverton and Mario Batali's blistered-crust pizzas: the room that reset LA pizza.
Daniele Uditi's neo-Neapolitan pizza: soft, charred, and quietly perfect.
Steve Samson's Bolognese cooking: handmade pasta and a warm, cavernous downtown room.
Bright, inventive Southeast-Asian cooking in a leafy garden room: fresh and easy to love.
A small, sincere pasta room doing handmade Italian classics on the Westside.
Cantonese dim sum of real refinement: a San Gabriel Valley institution, fairly priced.
Richard Meier's travertine acropolis above the city: a world-class art collection, gardens and the view, all free.
The city's balcony to the stars: Art Deco domes, the planetarium, and the finest view of Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign.
A Roman country house recreated above the Pacific: Greek and Roman antiquities in a garden of fountains.

venues.n: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
venues.d: The largest art museum in the western United States, and Chris Burden's Urban Light, the city's most photographed lamps.
Frank Gehry's billowing steel masterpiece: home of the LA Philharmonic and the icon of downtown.
A honeycomb-veiled museum of contemporary art: Koons, Warhol and Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms.
A railway magnate's estate of libraries, art and 120 acres of botanical gardens: a Gutenberg Bible among the roses.
The end of Route 66 over the Pacific: the Ferris wheel, the sand, and the quintessential Californian sunset.

venues.n: Hollywood: Walk of Fame, Chinese Theatre & the Sign
venues.d: The centre of the movie myth: the terrazzo stars, the handprints at Grauman's, and the Sign on the hill above.
The most famous luxury shopping street in the world: the flagships of every great house, in three gilded blocks.

venues.n: The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
venues.d: The definitive museum of cinema, in a Renzo Piano sphere: the art and machinery of the movies.

venues.n: The Broad Stage & Bergamot / Venice Canals & Boardwalk
venues.d: The bohemian edge of the city: the canals Abbot Kinney dug, the muscle-beach boardwalk, and Abbot Kinney's shops.

venues.n: Runyon Canyon & the Hollywood Hills trails
venues.d: The city's favourite hillside walk: a short, steep climb to a panorama of the whole basin.
The birthplace of Los Angeles: the oldest quarter of the city, and a lively Mexican marketplace.
A rooftop mezcal-and-agave temple over Los Feliz: the highest-ranked bar in Los Angeles.
A breezy, boundary-pushing SoCal cocktail bar: laboratory technique with a Southern soul.
The New York cocktail institution's LA home: impeccable drinks in the Arts District.
A Filipina-run gin bar of real character: one of the city's most distinctive drinking rooms.
A speakeasy-style hideaway beneath a restaurant: intimate, low-lit, seriously made drinks.

venues.n: The Tower Bar, Sunset Tower Hotel
venues.d: Old-Hollywood glamour in Bugsy Siegel's former apartment: the most storied nightcap on the Strip.
A drink in the most legendary hotel in Hollywood: discreet, dimly lit, endlessly mythologised.

venues.n: The Polo Lounge, The Beverly Hills Hotel
venues.d: The power-lunch and nightcap of Beverly Hills since 1941: pink banquettes under the tropical garden.
The New York World's-Best bar transplanted to a Maybourne rooftop: negronis with a view.
